transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start time: 16:00 UTC (11:00 PT)
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees (as on call): Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood CSM), Dr. Lina Zhao (Silverleaf), Carlos Mendes (Silverleaf CTO), Priya Varma (Silverleaf Compliance), Samir Kaur (Silverleaf Infra)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):
- Customer nearing renewal window; wants to extend contract and run an APAC pilot (Singapore) before committing to multi-region uplift.
- Main asks: latency targets for telehealth chat, data residency in Singapore, compatibility with customer KMS, and pricing for pilot + reserved uplift.
- Redwood to send revised quote and schedule technical deep dive on VPC/KMS integration.

Topics: renewal timing, APAC pilot, private/VPC requirements, SOC2/KMS, latency targets, burst capacity, canary rollouts, pricing model.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight — running through renewal options and the Singapore pilot ask. quick intro round?
[00:08] Lina (Silverleaf): Hi, Lina here, head of MLOps, I've got Samir and Priya with me, Carlos is on as well.
[00:12] Carlos: yep, hello.
[00:15] Ethan (Redwood): Ethan, SE — I'll lead the tech bits, happy to dig into latency/capacity.
[00:20] Maya: cool. quick agenda: 1) renewal timeline and contract amendment, 2) APAC pilot scope (singapore), 3) security/KMS/VPC notes, 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Priya: perfect.

[00:45] Carlos: to start — high level we like Redwood, usage has grown 3x last quarter, we're up for renewal in ~45 days and want to add a pilot in APAC before we sign a longer uplift. want to understand cost if we add reserved nodes vs just burst capacity.
[01:05] Maya: understood. short answer: reserved gives best unit economics and guaranteed throughput; burst is cheaper up front but no SLA. we can model both. we'll include an APAC pilot pricing line in the quote.
[01:20] Lina: the pilot is for Singapore region only to validate latency for live telehealth chat — target p95 < 200ms for short prompts; throughput initial 60 concurrent streams, scale to 180 within 2 weeks if ok.
[01:38] Ethan: got it — p95 200ms is realistic with region-local serving but depends on model size and quantization. what models are you planning to use?
[01:50] Carlos: primarily a trimmed gpt-like open model we quantized in-house (8-bit). some flows use system prompts that hit 1-2k tokens occasionally.
[02:04] Ethan: big consideration: KV cache and continuous batching. with short back-and-forth chat, cache hits should help, but those 1–2k bursts will increase mem usage — we can recommend a quantization profile and kernel set that keeps latency under target.
[02:20] Samir: are there known issues with our quantized model and Redwood runtime? last time one of the ops runs had weird tokenization timing.
[02:28] Ethan: there's occasional tokenization alignment differences between model exports — we'll run a compatibility job in staging. I'll take the model artifact and run a quick perf baseline.

[02:45] Priya: compliance: need to confirm data residency in Singapore and customer-managed keys (we use an HSM-backed KMS). also SOC2 evidence and encryption in transit at rest.
[02:58] Maya: yes — for Private deployments we can support KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) and we have SOC2 Type II report — will share redacted version. for Hosted we have options for region isolation but not BYOK unless we do Dedicated/Private.
[03:15] Priya: so BYOK is only with Private? or can Dedicated pairs integrate with our KMS?
[03:22] Ethan: Dedicated can often integrate with customer KMS depending on the cloud provider and network setup; Private (VPC) gives the most control. we should scope it in the technical deep dive.

[03:40] Carlos: cost tradeoffs — if we do Private for Singapore-only pilot, what's the baseline operational lift? we don't want full on-prem.
[03:50] Maya: Private VPC package for a pilot is smaller footprint — we offer a pilot package with a limited node pool and an onboarding fee. ops lift mostly on network peering and KMS setup; Redwood runs the control plane, but customer manages keys and networking.
[04:05] Samir: peering to our VPC in SG will need firewall rules; we also want a canary rollout so only a subset of traffic goes to SG region initially. does Redwood support route-level canaries?
[04:16] Ethan: yes, routing policies support percentage split by route, model version pinning, and automatic fallback to a global hosted model if the region capacity is exhausted. we can set up a canary that starts at 5% and ramps to 20% then 100% over two weeks.

[04:35] Lina: one more nit — we have HIPAA-adjacent data in some transcripts; Priya will need to confirm the compliance posture. does Redwood encrypt logs at rest and provide audit logs?
[04:45] Maya: audit logs, retention controls, and role-based access are in our enterprise package. logs can be routed to your SIEM and we support encryption at rest and in transit. we'll add the SOC2 docs and an audit log sample.

[05:00] (small cross-talk about timezones and who's covering APAC support)

[05:25] Carlos: another technical ask — cold start for the model in SG: what warm-up strategies do you recommend for predictable latency?
[05:33] Ethan: pre-warming with pinned instances plus KV prefix priming for common prompts. we can also use predictive keepalive for expected traffic windows (e.g., clinic hours). warm starts take a couple seconds for large models unless using pinned GPU). with pinned reserved nodes you can have near-constant hot caches.

[05:55] Priya: encryption for keys — we need to know if Redwood ever sees plaintext keys and the HSM flow.
[06:02] Maya: we never persist your keys in our control plane. KMS handshake is done via customer-owned HSM and we use ephemeral handles. I'll include a short KMS integration note with the runbook.

[06:20] Carlos: what's the SLA for Dedicated vs Private? we need to know uptime and latency windows.
[06:26] Maya: Dedicated comes with 99.95% uptime and latency SLOs per route we can agree on in the SLA; Private can be negotiated for managed SLAs, but since network peering adds variables we commonly split responsibilities for network uptime vs service.

[06:45] Lina: ok. timeline: we want a pilot starting second week of December, two-week run, then decision by mid-December to finalize renewal. is that feasible?
[06:55] Maya: yes, tight but feasible — we need signed amendment and PO by Dec 5th to provision reserved test capacity for Dec 8th start.

[07:10] (brief pause)

[07:20] Ethan: tech deep dive notes: I'll need the model artifact, tokenization metadata, sample prompts (esp. multi-turn telehealth flows), and expected concurrency. please also share your current prefix reuse ratios if available.
[07:35] Samir: we can share telemetry from our staging cluster — p95 baseline etc.

[07:45] Maya: I'll also call out pricing options: 1) short APAC pilot as a time-limited reserved mini-pool, 2) pay-as-you-go burst with auto-scaling, 3) immediate reserved uplift for multi-region with discounted unit rates. We'll show numbers side-by-side.

[08:00] Priya: and the legal — we need contract language on data residency and subprocessor list.
[08:06] Maya: yes we'll include subprocessor list and a data processing addendum. privacy addendum will be included in the amendment.

[08:20] Carlos: small thing — we've seen tokenization mismatches cause small hallucination regressions in the field, any guardrails?
[08:29] Ethan: recommend a quick eval harness (unit tests) that checks output for critical prompts, plus a small set of safety checks in the pipeline. Redwood also supports eval hooks to trigger alerts when quality regresses vs baseline.

[08:45] Lina: thanks, that's helpful.

[09:00] Action items recap (auto):
- Redwood: price lines + pilot quote, SOC2 redacted, data processing addendum, KMS runbook.
- Redwood SE: baseline perf run on provided model artifact and VPC integration checklist.
- Silverleaf: provide traffic profile, sample prompts, HIPAA scope confirmation, and PO decision timeline.

[09:25] (a short side conversation about internal approvals on Silverleaf side; faint audio)

[09:50] Carlos: one more question — if pilot shows latency issues we might want to fall back to a smaller distilled model in APAC while keeping heavier models in hosted region. is that supported?
[10:00] Ethan: yes, routing policy can send requests to a distilled variant by route or by percentage. we can also do automated fallback if latency/p95 exceeds threshold.

[10:15] Priya: please send the SOC2 and the redacted subprocessor list — we need to start legal review this week.
[10:22] Maya: will do.

[10:30] (wrap up)
[10:35] Maya: next steps recap: we'll send revised quote 11/28, schedule the tech deep dive for week of 12/1 (Ethan + Samir + Lina), and target a pilot start 12/08 pending PO. Priya will confirm compliance items by 11/30.
[10:55] Carlos: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:00] Lina: thanks.

(End of meeting)

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a few words mistranscribed (tokenization -> tokenization timing; HSM sometimes appears as 'H S M' in auto text), some speaker labels defaulted to first names only.
